page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server configured with an Intel Xeon 6448H processor. This x86_64 CPU features 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz under a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, offering 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in LLM inference workloads. For a small 135M model, the server achieves prompt processing speeds of 13631.52 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 610.8 tokens per second. With a medium 7B model, prompt processing registers at 6293.73 tokens per second and text generation at 153.1 tokens per second. CPU performance is solid, with a Passmark CPU score of 40930.36 and a strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 15.59 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks reaches 173.77 GB/sec for reads and 66.7 GB/sec for writes.

The hardware profile offers high resource density, combining a massive 180.0 GB memory footprint with a high-capacity 48 GB VRAM GPU, which is highly cost-efficient for medium-scale AI workloads without requiring multi-GPU clusters. However, the shared CPU allocation model and a modest 2.0 GHz base clock speed represent a tradeoff for workloads heavily reliant on dedicated, high-frequency single-core performance. This server is optimized for LLM inference, machine learning model training, data science pipelines, and database operations requiring local NVMe storage.
description: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server designed for memory-intensive and accelerated computing workloads. It features an Intel Xeon 6448H processor with 16 vCPUs and 16 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz, paired with 180.0 GB of system memory. Graphics and parallel processing are handled by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU with 48 GB of Ada Lovelace VRAM. Local storage is supported by a 1200 GB NVMe SSD. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier LLM inference capabilities, processing 6293.73 tokens per second for prompt processing on a medium 7B model. While the shared CPU allocation is a tradeoff for pure compute-bound tasks, the high VRAM and system memory density make it highly cost-efficient for machine learning, data science, and database workloads.
